## Proof

We claim
$$\lim_{|r|\to\infty}\int_{\mathbb{R}}|f(x+r)+f(x)|^p\,dx \;=\; 2\,\|f\|_p^p \;=\; 2\int_{\mathbb{R}}|f(x)|^p\,dx.$$

**Step 1: The case $f\in C_c(\mathbb{R})$.**

Suppose $f$ is continuous with compact support, say $\operatorname{supp} f \subseteq [-M,M]$. Then $\operatorname{supp}(f(\cdot+r)) \subseteq [-M-r,\, M-r]$. For $|r|>2M$ the two supports are disjoint, hence at every $x\in\mathbb{R}$ at most one of $f(x+r)$, $f(x)$ is nonzero. Consequently
$$|f(x+r)+f(x)|^p = |f(x+r)|^p + |f(x)|^p \quad\text{a.e.}$$
and by translation-invariance of Lebesgue measure,
$$\int_{\mathbb{R}}|f(x+r)+f(x)|^p\,dx = \int_{\mathbb{R}}|f(x+r)|^p\,dx + \int_{\mathbb{R}}|f(x)|^p\,dx = 2\|f\|_p^p.$$

**Step 2: Reduction to the compactly supported case.**

Let $f\in L^p(\mathbb{R})$ and fix $\varepsilon>0$. Since $C_c(\mathbb{R})$ is dense in $L^p(\mathbb{R})$ for $1\le p<\infty$, choose $g\in C_c(\mathbb{R})$ with $\|f-g\|_p<\varepsilon$. Set $h:=f-g$, so $\|h\|_p<\varepsilon$.

Write
$$f(\cdot+r)+f = \bigl[g(\cdot+r)+g\bigr] + \bigl[h(\cdot+r)+h\bigr].$$
By Minkowski's inequality,
$$\bigl|\,\|f(\cdot+r)+f\|_p - \|g(\cdot+r)+g\|_p\,\bigr| \le \|h(\cdot+r)+h\|_p \le 2\|h\|_p < 2\varepsilon. \tag{1}$$

By Step 1, for all $|r|$ sufficiently large (say $|r|>R_0$, where $R_0$ depends only on $\operatorname{supp} g$),
$$\|g(\cdot+r)+g\|_p^p = 2\,\|g\|_p^p, \qquad\text{i.e.}\qquad \|g(\cdot+r)+g\|_p = 2^{1/p}\|g\|_p. \tag{2}$$

Also $\bigl|\|f\|_p-\|g\|_p\bigr|\le\|h\|_p<\varepsilon$, so
$$\|g\|_p \in \bigl[\|f\|_p-\varepsilon,\;\|f\|_p+\varepsilon\bigr]. \tag{3}$$

**Step 3: Taking the limit.**

Combining (1), (2), (3): for $|r|>R_0$,
$$\|f(\cdot+r)+f\|_p \;\in\; \bigl[\,2^{1/p}\|g\|_p-2\varepsilon,\; 2^{1/p}\|g\|_p+2\varepsilon\,\bigr] \;\subseteq\; \bigl[\,2^{1/p}\|f\|_p-(2+2^{1/p})\varepsilon,\; 2^{1/p}\|f\|_p+(2+2^{1/p})\varepsilon\,\bigr].$$

Since $\varepsilon>0$ was arbitrary,
$$\lim_{|r|\to\infty}\|f(\cdot+r)+f\|_p = 2^{1/p}\|f\|_p.$$

The map $t\mapsto t^p$ is continuous on $[0,\infty)$, so raising to the $p$-th power gives
$$\lim_{|r|\to\infty}\|f(\cdot+r)+f\|_p^p = \bigl(2^{1/p}\|f\|_p\bigr)^p = 2\,\|f\|_p^p.$$

That is,
$$\boxed{\displaystyle\lim_{|r|\to\infty}\int_{\mathbb{R}}|f(x+r)+f(x)|^p\,dx = 2\int_{\mathbb{R}}|f(x)|^p\,dx.}$$
